trials.name: INVOKE-2
trials.population: Adult participants aged 50-85 with early Alzheimer's disease and evidence of brain amyloidosis, excluding APOE e4/e4 homozygotes.
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score at Weeks 24, 48, 72 and 96.
trials.results_summary: The study failed to meet its primary endpoint (CDR-SB) and showed no significant differences on any secondary cognitive or functional endpoints compared to placebo. Treatment was associated with notably increased incidences of ARIA-E and ARIA-H.

trials.population: Participants with early Alzheimer's disease who completed the planned treatment period in the parent INVOKE-2 study (NCT04592874).
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety and Tolerability as Measured by Number of Treatment-expected Adverse Events (TEAE) and Treatment-related Adverse Events (AEs).
trials.results_summary: This open-label extension was terminated early due to the negative efficacy and safety results from the parent INVOKE-2 trial.

trials.population: Healthy volunteers and participants with probable Alzheimer's disease dementia.
trials.primary_endpoint: Evaluation of safety and tolerability of AL002 measured by number of subjects with adverse events and Dose Limiting Adverse Event (DLAEs)
trials.results_summary: First-in-human trial demonstrated that AL002 was generally safe and tolerable, showing target engagement in the central nervous system by reducing soluble TREM2.

related_evidence.description: Peer-reviewed publication of the Phase 2 randomized trial of AL002 in Nature Medicine, confirming negative primary and secondary endpoints alongside increased ARIA rates.
ClinicalTrials.gov posted results for the AL002 INVOKE-2 Phase 2 study.
Preclinical and first-in-human Phase 1 evaluation of AL002 published in Alzheimer's Research & Therapy.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence strongly corroborates the document's claims that AL002 is neither effective at slowing cognitive decline nor safe regarding amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) in early Alzheimer's disease. The Phase 2 INVOKE-2 trial (NCT04592874) decisively failed its primary endpoint (CDR-SB) and all secondary cognitive/functional endpoints, while demonstrating a dose-dependent increase in ARIA-E and ARIA-H. These negative findings were confirmed by the subsequent early termination of the AL002 long-term extension study (NCT05744401) and the formal peer-reviewed publication of the trial results in Nature Medicine in 2026. Consequently, clinical development of AL002 for Alzheimer's disease has been effectively halted.
discrepancies: The analyzed document reports an enrollment of 356 participants based on the ClinicalTrials.gov registry extract, whereas the subsequent peer-reviewed publication in Nature Medicine (May 2026) reports that 381 participants were randomized.
